entries.description: In `on enchant`: the enchantments the table adds, like `sharpness 3`. Read only.
entries.example:
on enchant:
    send "%applied enchantments%" to player
entries.name: Applied enchantments

entries.description: A command argument, counted from 1. Its type comes from the command line.
entries.example:
command /pay <player> <number>:
    trigger:
        send "Paying %arg-2% to %arg-1%"
entries.name: Argument

entries.description: Math with the usual order. Works on timespans and dates too. Dividing by zero is a runtime error.
entries.example: set {_half} to (5 + 3) / 2
entries.name: Arithmetic

entries.description: The loom item for a banner pattern type such as `creeper`, `flower`, `globe`, `mojang`, `piglin`, `skull`, `flow`, `guster`, `field_masoned` or `bordure_indented`. Gives none for patterns that have no item.
entries.example: give 1 of banner pattern item of "creeper" to player
entries.name: Banner pattern item

entries.description: In `on piglin barter`: the item the piglin took and the items it will throw.
entries.example:
on piglin barter:
    broadcast "%barter drops%"
entries.name: Barter input / drops

entries.description: The effect a beacon gives (`speed`), or `<none>`. Read only; Pumpkin 0.2.2 has no way to pick beacon effects in game.
entries.example: send "%primary beacon effect of location(0, 64, 0, world "world")%"
entries.name: Beacon effects

entries.description: Where the player respawns, the same as `respawn location`. Can be set.
entries.example: set player's bed location to location(0, 70, 0)
entries.name: Bed location

entries.description: The honey level (0 to 5) of a beehive or bee nest block; `max` gives 5. Can be set, added to, removed from and reset (to 0); results stay between 0 and 5.
entries.example: set honey level of block at location(0, 64, 0) to 5
entries.name: Beehive honey level

entries.description: A block position. `targeted block` looks up to 100 blocks.
entries.example: set {_b} to block below player
entries.name: Block

entries.description: The block id and its state properties as a text like `oak_log[axis=y]`. Setting it places the block and its properties; properties not named keep their value.
entries.example: set block data of block at location(0, 64, 0) to "oak_log[axis=x]"
entries.name: Block data

entries.description: Every block whose center is within the radius, as block locations. The radius goes up to 32.
entries.name: Block sphere

entries.description: The block type as an item, like `stone`.
entries.example: send "You stand on %type of block below player%." to player
entries.name: Block type

entries.description: `between`: every block of the box (up to 262144). `from ... to`: the blocks a straight line passes through. A direction: the 100 blocks next to the location that way.
entries.example:
loop blocks from player to location(0, 64, 0):
    set block at loop-value to glass
entries.name: Blocks

entries.description: The author, title and pages of a written book. They work on the held item (`player's tool`) and can be set; setting them on any held item makes it carry book content.
entries.example:
set book title of player's tool to "Rules"
set page 1 of player's tool to "Be nice"
entries.name: Book author, title and pages

entries.description: A true or false value.
entries.example: set {_on} to true
entries.name: Boolean

entries.description: The id of the boss bar with that id, or none when there is no such bar. Carve names bars by their text id, so the result works anywhere a bar id does.
entries.name: Boss bar from key

entries.description: The id of a boss bar when it exists, and its progress from 0 to 100.
entries.example:
create bossbar "raid" with progress 40
send "%progress of bossbar "raid"%"
entries.name: Boss bar key and progress

entries.description: An item in a brewing stand, read from and written to the block entity data. Can be set.
entries.example: set ingredient slot of block at {_stand} to nether wart
entries.name: Brewing stand slot

entries.description: The message in `on broadcast` (the same as `event-text`). Read only.
entries.example:
on broadcast:
    send "[log] %broadcast message%" to console
entries.name: Broadcast message

entries.description: How far a suspicious sand or gravel block has been brushed (0 to 3); `max` gives 3. Can be set, added to, removed from and reset.
entries.example: send "%brushing stage of block at location(0, 64, 0)%"
entries.name: Brushing stage

entries.description: The chat text. Only in `on chat`.
entries.example:
on chat:
    send "You said: %message%" to player
entries.name: Chat message

entries.description: A new, empty chest inventory value: 1 to 6 rows (3 when not given), titled `Chest` when not named. Keep it in a variable, fill it with `set slot`, then `open` it. Copies are the same inventory, so `event-inventory is {shop}` works.
entries.example:
set {_gui} to chest inventory with 3 rows named "Shop"
set slot 4 of {_gui} to diamond named "&bBuy"
open {_gui} to player
entries.name: Chest inventory

entries.description: A chunk value, or the list of chunks in a square radius (at most 32).
entries.example:
on join:
    set {_c::*} to chunks in radius 1 around player
    send "%size of {_c::*}%"
entries.name: Chunk

entries.description: In click events: the clicked block type as an item (`air` for air).
entries.name: Clicked block

entries.description: The weather only this player sees: `rain`, `clear`, or `<none>` when it follows the world. Set it with `set client weather of player to rain` and `reset client weather of player`.
entries.example:
set client weather of player to rain
send "%client weather of player%"
entries.name: Client weather

entries.description: Turns color codes and tags into `§` codes, or strips them all.
entries.example: set {_plain} to uncolored "<red>Hello"
entries.name: Colored / uncolored

entries.description: The item in `on consume` (the same as `event-item`). Read only.
entries.example:
on consume:
    send "you ate %consumed item%"
entries.name: Consumed item

entries.description: One coordinate of a location or player.
entries.example: send "You are at y %y of player%" to player
entries.name: Coordinates

entries.description: In `on damage` and `on death`: the hurt or dead mob. With a type (`the zombie`) it is none when the mob is another type. Players are `player` and `victim`.
entries.name: Creature / entity / typed event entity

entries.description: The item on the cursor in `on inventory click`, before the click. Read only.
entries.example:
on inventory click:
    send "holding %cursor slot of player%"
entries.name: Cursor slot

entries.description: How much durability an item has used up, and how much it has left. Can be set, reset, added to and removed from on the held item (`player's tool`).
entries.example:
set damage of player's tool to 0
send "%durability of player's tool% uses left"
entries.name: Damage value and durability

entries.description: In `on damage` and `on death`: the damage of the hit, the attacking player or entity and the hurt player or entity. `attacker is a zombie`, `type of attacker` and `name of attacker` (the custom name, else the type) work on entities.
entries.name: Damage values

entries.description: An item with that much durability used up.
entries.example: give diamond sword with damage 500 to player
entries.name: Damaged item

entries.description: Removes the first value (or the first N values) from a queue variable and gives them. The variable keeps the rest. An empty queue gives none.
entries.example: set {_next} to dequeue {_queue}
entries.name: De-queue

entries.description: The first value, or the second when the first is not set.
entries.example: send "Coins: %{coins::%uuid of player%} ? 0%" to player
entries.name: Default value

entries.description: The display or tab list name, falling back to the account name.
entries.example: send "Hi %display name of player%" to player
entries.name: Display and tab list name

entries.description: The distance between two locations or players.
entries.example: set {_d} to distance between player and location(0, 64, 0)
entries.name: Distance

entries.description: In `on enchant` and `on enchant prepare`: the item, in `on enchant` the level cost and the enchantment (and level) the table showed, in `on enchant prepare` the bookshelf bonus. Read only.
entries.example:
on enchant:
    send "%enchant item% for %exp cost% levels: %enchantment hint%"
entries.name: Enchant item, cost, bonus and hint

entries.description: The level of an enchantment written like `sharpness 5` or `sharpness V` (1 when there is no number), or of an enchantment offer.
entries.example: send "%enchantment level of "sharpness 5"%"
entries.name: Enchantment level

entries.description: In `on enchant prepare`: the offers of the table (1-3), as values with an enchantment, a level and a cost. Read only.
entries.example:
on enchant prepare:
    send "%enchantment offer 1%"
entries.name: Enchantment offer

entries.description: The level cost of an enchantment offer.
entries.example:
on enchant prepare:
    send "%cost of enchantment offer 1% levels"
entries.name: Enchantment offer cost

entries.description: The items in a player's ender chest, and one slot of it (0-26, can be set). `open player's ender chest to player` and `clear ender chest of player` work too; Pumpkin can only show players their own ender chest.
entries.example:
set slot 0 of ender chest of player to diamond
open player's ender chest to player
entries.name: Ender chest

entries.description: The block an enderman holds, as block data text. Can be set to a block type or block data, and reset.
entries.example:
spawn an enderman at player
set carried block of last spawned entity to "tnt"
entries.name: Enderman carrying block data

entries.description: Whether a mob's AI is on. Can be set to true or false. Players have none.
entries.example:
spawn a zombie at player
set ai of last spawned entity to false
entries.name: Entity AI

entries.description: The base value of an attribute (`movement speed`, `max health`, `scale`, ...), or with `total` the value with modifiers. Can be set, reset, added to and removed from (that changes the base).
entries.example:
set movement speed attribute of player to 0.2
reset scale attribute of player
entries.name: Entity attribute

entries.description: In `on mob spawn`: the entity type as text, and why it spawned.
entries.name: Event entity

entries.description: In `on inventory click`: the menu Carve opened, with its name and live contents. `clicked inventory` is `<none>` when the click was in the player's own inventory below the menu. Both are `<none>` for windows Carve did not open.
entries.name: Event inventory

entries.description: The item of a drop, pick up, consume or craft event.
entries.example:
on drop:
    send "dropped %event-item%" to player
entries.name: Event item

entries.description: The location of a projectile hit or mob spawn.
entries.example:
on projectile hit:
    strike lightning effect at event-location
entries.name: Event location

entries.description: In `on craft`: the recipe id without `minecraft:`.
entries.example:
on craft:
    send "%event-recipe%" to player
entries.name: Event recipe

entries.description: The items for which the test holds. `input` is the item being tested.
entries.example:
set {_n::*} to 1, 5 and 9
set {_big::*} to {_n::*} where [input > 2]
entries.name: Filtered list

entries.description: Part of a list variable: the first or last N values, or the values from position N to M (1-based, inclusive). Asking for more than the list holds gives what there is.
entries.example: send "%first 3 elements of {top::*}%"
entries.name: First, last and ranges of elements

entries.description: Food level and saturation, 0 to 20.
entries.example:
if food level of player < 6:
    send "You are hungry." to player
entries.name: Food and saturation

entries.description: A date as text, Java-style format letters. Default `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`.
entries.example: send "It is %now formatted as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"%" to player
entries.name: Formatted date

entries.description: The player's game mode as text.
entries.example: send "%gamemode of player%" to player
entries.name: Gamemode

entries.description: Current or max health (20 = 10 hearts).
entries.example: send "%health of player% / %max health of player%" to player
entries.name: Health

entries.description: In `on projectile hit`: the player that was hit, or `<none>`.
entries.name: Hit player

entries.description: Where a text appears, from 1. 0 when not found. Case sensitive.
entries.example: send "%index of "l" in "hello"%" to player
entries.name: Index of

entries.description: What the click in `on inventory click` does, like `pickup all`, `place one`, `swap with cursor`, `move to other inventory` or `drop one slot`. Worked out from the click type, the clicked item and the cursor.
entries.name: Inventory action

entries.description: In `on inventory click`: the slot number, the item in it and the kind of click.
entries.example:
on inventory click:
    send "%click type% on %clicked slot%" to player
entries.name: Inventory click values

entries.description: Rows and slots of a chest inventory value, the players who have it open, and its holder (always none for chests made by scripts).
entries.example:
set {_g} to chest inventory with 3 rows named "Shop"
send "%rows of {_g}%"
entries.name: Inventory rows, slots, holder and viewers

entries.description: The item in a slot, unset when empty. Slots count from 0.
entries.example: set {_item} to slot 3 of player's current inventory
entries.name: Inventory slot

entries.description: A Minecraft item id with spaces, optionally with an amount. Checked at load.
entries.example: give 16 oak logs to player
entries.name: Item

entries.description: An item value with a component set, for `give`.
entries.example: give diamond sword with custom model data 7 to player
entries.name: Item with component

entries.description: Every item in an inventory value, `event-inventory` or a player's inventory (armor and off hand included), as a list. Empty slots are left out.
entries.example:
loop items in player's inventory:
    send "%loop-value%" to player
entries.name: Items in

entries.description: One text from a list. Unset items are skipped.
entries.example:
set {_l::*} to "a" and "b"
send join {_l::*} with ", " to player
entries.name: Join list

entries.description: The number of characters.
entries.example: send "%length of "hello"%" to player
entries.name: Length

entries.description: Whole levels, total experience points, or progress to the next level (0 to 1).
entries.example: send "You are level %level of player%" to player
entries.name: Level and experience

entries.description: Items of a list by position, at random, or its indices.
entries.example: send "%random element of {_l::*}%" to player
entries.name: List elements

entries.description: Several values in a row. Used with `set`, `add`, `remove` and `loop`.
entries.example: set {_colors::*} to "red", "green" and "blue"
entries.name: List literal

entries.description: A point in a world. Without a world, a teleport keeps the player in theirs.
entries.example: set {spawn} to location of player
entries.name: Location

entries.description: Values of the current loop: the item, the player, the list index, the count or the round number.
entries.example:
loop 3 times:
    send "%loop-number%" to player
entries.name: Loop values

entries.description: Plain records for loot data. Carve can't roll a loot table, so these only carry values around.
entries.example: set {_c} to loot context at player's location with luck 2
entries.name: Loot tables and loot contexts
patterns: loot context at %location% [with luck %number%] [with looter %player%] [with looted entity %player%]

entries.description: The blocks or items in a vanilla tag such as "logs", or the tags a block or item belongs to. The tag list is built in.
entries.example:
on join:
    set {_l::*} to minecraft block tag "logs"
    send "%size of {_l::*}%"
entries.name: Minecraft tag

entries.description: The lowest (always 1) and highest vanilla level of an enchantment.
entries.example: send "%max enchantment level of sharpness%"
entries.name: Minimum and maximum enchantment level

entries.description: The list 1, 2, ... N.
entries.example: set {_l::*} to 3 times
entries.name: N times

entries.description: The player's name as text.
entries.example: set {owner} to name of player
entries.name: Name

entries.description: A potion effect value to keep in a variable and apply later with `apply {_e} to player`. Without a tier it is 1; without `for` it lasts 15 seconds.
entries.example:
set {_e} to potion effect of speed of tier 2 for 30 seconds
apply {_e} to player
entries.name: New potion effect
patterns: [a[n]] [ambient] potion effect of %potion effect type% [[of] tier %number%] [without particles] [for %timespan%]
[an] (infinite|permanent) [ambient] potion effect of %potion effect type% [[of] tier %number%]

entries.description: A line break, text without outer spaces, or text backwards.
entries.example: send "line one%nl%line two" to player
entries.name: Newline, trimmed, reversed

entries.description: The current date (UTC), a date from a unix timestamp in seconds, or the timestamp of a date.
entries.example: set {last::%uuid of player%} to now
entries.name: Now and unix dates

entries.description: A number like `5` or `-2.5`. Prints at most 4 decimals.
entries.example: set {_a} to 10
entries.name: Number

entries.description: In `on gamemode change`: the mode before and after.
entries.example:
on gamemode change:
    send "%old gamemode% to %new gamemode%" to player
entries.name: Old and new gamemode

entries.description: In `on level change`: the level before and after.
entries.example:
on level change:
    send "now level %new level%" to player
entries.name: Old and new level

entries.description: The reason the kicked player sees, in `on kick`. Read only on Pumpkin.
entries.example:
on kick:
    broadcast "%player% was kicked: %on-screen kick message%"
entries.name: On-screen kick message

entries.description: The value of an option from the file's `options:` block.
entries.example:
options:
    price: 25
on join:
    send "That costs {@price} coins." to player
entries.name: Option

entries.description: Replaces every `%name%` placeholder in the text. Write `%%name%%` in a script string, because `%%` is a literal percent sign there. Unknown placeholders stay as written.
entries.example: send parse placeholders in "Hi %%player_name%%, %%server_online%% online" for player
entries.name: Parse placeholders

entries.description: A whole number, true or false (`yes` and `on` count), or an online player from text. `<none>` if the text does not fit.
entries.example: set {_b} to "yes" parsed as boolean
entries.name: Parsed as integer, boolean or player

entries.description: The number in a text, or `<none>` if it isn't one.
entries.example: set {_n} to "42" parsed as number
entries.name: Parsed as number

entries.description: Parts of a particle value. They can be set on a variable: `set particle count of {_p} to 5`.
entries.example:
set {_p} to flame particle
set particle count of {_p} to 5
send "%particle count of {_p}%"
entries.name: Particle count, offset and speed

entries.description: A particle with its count, offset and speed, to keep in a variable and draw with `draw {_p} at <place>`. With a velocity the count is 0 and the vector is the direction.
entries.example:
set {_p} to flame particle with offset vector(1, 0, 1) with particle speed 0.1
draw {_p} at player
entries.name: Particle value

entries.description: The keys of the persistent data Carve scripts stored on a player, entity, block or item, sorted.
entries.example: send "%persistent data keys of player%"
entries.name: Persistent data keys

entries.description: The player's ping in milliseconds, or their IP address.
entries.example: send "Ping: %ping of player% ms" to player
entries.name: Ping and IP

entries.description: Value of one placeholder (no percent signs), like `"player_name"`, `"server_online"`, `"carve_var_coins"` or one a script defines. The player defaults to the event's player. Unknown placeholders give `<none>`.
entries.example: send placeholder "player_health" for player
entries.name: Placeholder

entries.description: Values inside `on placeholder request`. `the identifier` and `the prefix` are read only; `set the result to ...` answers the request.
entries.example:
on placeholder request for prefix "x":
    set the result to "you asked for %the identifier%"
entries.name: Placeholder request values

entries.description: The item without its name, lore and enchantments. Type and amount stay.
entries.example:
set {_i} to diamond sword
set {_p} to plain {_i}
entries.name: Plain item

entries.description: The player of the event, or who ran the command. `<none>` when offline or for the console.
entries.example: send "Hi %player%" to player
entries.name: Player

entries.description: A player head with that player's skin, for `give`.
entries.example: give skull of player to player
entries.name: Player skull

entries.description: How long until the entity can use a portal again, as a timespan. Can be set.
entries.example:
set portal cooldown of player to 7 seconds
send "%portal cooldown of player%" to player
entries.name: Portal cooldown

entries.description: Parts of a potion effect value. The amplifier starts at 0, the tier at 1. All three can be set on a variable: `set potion amplifier of {_e} to 2`.
entries.example:
set {_e} to potion effect of speed 2
send "%potion tier of {_e}% for %potion duration of {_e}%"
entries.name: Potion effect amplifier, tier and duration

entries.description: Whether an effect type is `beneficial`, `harmful` or `neutral`.
entries.example: send "%potion category of poison%"
entries.name: Potion effect type category

entries.description: The active potion effects of a player, one of them, or its tier. Players only.
entries.example:
send "%potion effects of player%"
send "%tier of speed of player%"
entries.name: Potion effects of a player

entries.description: A potion, splash potion or lingering potion item with that effect, for `give`.
entries.example: give splash potion of poison to player
entries.name: Potion item

entries.description: The force of the shot in `on entity shoot bow`. Pumpkin fires that event only for mobs.
entries.example:
on entity shoot bow:
    broadcast "force %projectile force%"
entries.name: Projectile force

entries.description: The protocol number of a Java player's client, or of the server when no player is given (777 for Minecraft 26.3).
entries.example: send "%protocol version of player% / %protocol version%" to player
entries.name: Protocol version

entries.description: A first-in first-out queue, and its first or last element without removing it.
entries.example:
set {_q} to a new queue of 1, 2 and 3
send "%start of {_q}%"
entries.name: Queue and its start and end

entries.description: A random whole number (both ends included) or decimal number.
entries.example: set {_roll} to random integer between 1 and 6
entries.name: Random number

entries.description: The namespaced id of an item, like `minecraft:diamond_sword`.
entries.example: send "%raw name of player's tool%"
entries.name: Raw name

entries.description: Casts a thin ray and keeps the result in a variable. The hit is the nearer of the first block and the first entity. From a location, give a direction.
entries.example:
on join:
    set {_r} to ray trace from player with max distance 50
    send "you look at %hit block of {_r}%"
entries.name: Ray trace
patterns: ray trace from %player|location% [in direction %vector%] [with max distance %number%] [including fluids] [ignoring blocks|entities|fluids]

entries.description: The power level read from a block's state: wire, weighted plates, targets and daylight detectors give their power, redstone blocks 15, levers, buttons, torches and repeaters 15 when on, anything else 0.
entries.example: send "%redstone power of targeted block of player%"
entries.name: Redstone power

entries.description: The text with the matches of a regular expression replaced.
entries.example: send "x1y2" with all regex "[0-9]" replaced with "_" to player
entries.name: Regex replaced text

entries.description: A new text with matches replaced.
entries.example: set {_t} to "a-b" with all "-" replaced with " "
entries.name: Replaced text

entries.description: Charges of a respawn anchor (0 to 4), or 4 for the maximum. Set with `set charges of <block> to 3`.
entries.example: send "%charges of targeted block of player%"
entries.name: Respawn anchor charges

entries.description: Why the player respawns, in `on respawn`: `death`, or `end_portal`.
entries.example:
on respawn:
    send "%respawn reason%"
entries.name: Respawn reason

entries.description: Calls a script function by its name and gives what it returns.
entries.example:
function double(n: number) :: number:
    return {_n} * 2

on join:
    send "%result of function "double" with arguments 21%"
entries.name: Result of a function

entries.description: How long a bell block has been ringing, as a timespan.
entries.example: set {_t} to ringing time of block at player
entries.name: Ringing time

entries.description: The angle (degrees) and unit axis of a quaternion, and a vector or quaternion turned around an axis by an angle in degrees.
entries.example: set {_v} to vector(1, 0, 0) rotated around z by 90
entries.name: Rotation angle, axis and rotated

entries.description: The scale attribute of a living entity or player (0.0625 to 16), or the transformation scale of a display entity (a vector). Can be set, added to, removed from and reset.
entries.example:
set scale of player to 2
reset scale of player
entries.name: Scale

entries.description: The pickle count of a sea pickle block (1 to 4); `min` and `max` are 1 and 4. The count can be set, added to and removed from.
entries.example: add 1 to sea pickles of block at location(0, 64, 0)
entries.name: Sea pickles

entries.description: Who started the trigger (a player or the console), the console itself, or the player.
entries.example: send "hello" to sender
entries.name: Sender

entries.description: Moves the world spawn with `setworldspawn`; only the main world can be set.
entries.example: set spawn of world "world" to location(7, 100, 7)
entries.name: Set world spawn

entries.description: Reads from the block entity data: the four front lines of a sign, the profile name and texture value of a skull, the entity a spawner spawns, and the loot table seed of a chest-like block. Unset values are none.
entries.example:
set {_lines::*} to sign text of block at player
set {_type} to spawner type of block at player
entries.name: Sign text, skull owner and texture, spawner type, loot table seed

entries.description: The number of direct items of a list.
entries.example: send "%size of {warps::*}% warps" to player
entries.name: Size of list

entries.description: The number of `clicked slot` or `slot N of <inventory>`.
entries.example: send "%index of slot 5 of player's inventory%"
entries.name: Slot index

entries.description: The item in a slot (0 is the top left) of an inventory value or `event-inventory`. Empty slots are `<none>`.
entries.example:
set {_gui} to chest inventory
send "%slot 0 of {_gui}%" to player
entries.name: Slot of an inventory value

entries.description: A copy of the list sorted by a key. `input` is each item while the key is worked out. Numbers, timespans and dates sort by value, text alphabetically. Items whose key is `<none>` go last.
entries.example:
set {_l::*} to "ccc", "a" and "bb"
send "%sorted {_l::*} by length of input%" to player
entries.name: Sorted by

entries.description: A reordered copy of a list.
entries.example:
set {_n::*} to 3, 1 and 2
set {_s::*} to sorted {_n::*}
entries.name: Sorted, reversed, shuffled

entries.description: Skript names for event values: the spreading block in `on spread`, the owner in `on tame`, the shooting entity in `on shoot` and the reason in `on spawn`.
entries.example:
on tame:
    broadcast "%tamer% tamed a pet"
entries.name: Source block, tamer, shooter, spawning reason

entries.description: The entity type a spawn egg makes. Setting it turns an item kept in a variable into another spawn egg.
entries.example:
set {_e} to 1 zombie spawn egg
set spawn egg entity of {_e} to "cow"
entries.name: Spawn egg entity

entries.description: The entity whose view a player sees. Set it to an entity; reset gives the player their own view back.
entries.example:
spawn a pig at player
set spectator target of player to last spawned entity
entries.name: Spectator target

entries.description: A list from a text. Works in `set {x::*} to` and `loop`.
entries.example: set {_parts::*} to split "a,b,c" at ","
entries.name: Split text

entries.description: The enchantments kept in an enchanted book in the main hand, as texts like `sharpness 5`. Set them to a text or a list of texts, or delete them.
entries.example: set stored enchantments of player's tool to "sharpness 5"
entries.name: Stored enchantments

entries.description: Pieces of a text. Positions count from 1.
entries.example: send "%first 3 characters of "hello"%" to player
entries.name: Substring

entries.description: Numbers from a list. Non-numbers are skipped.
entries.example:
set {_n::*} to 1, 5 and 9
send "%sum of {_n::*}%" to player
entries.name: Sum, average, min, max

entries.description: What a mob attacks, or the entity a player looks at (up to 100 blocks). Set it on mobs; delete or reset clears it. In `on target` plain `target` is the event's target.
entries.example: send "you look at %target of player%"
entries.name: Target

entries.description: The temperature at a block: the biome's base temperature, lower above y 80 as in vanilla (without vanilla's noise).
entries.example: send "%temperature of block below player%"
entries.name: Temperature

entries.description: Text in double quotes. `%...%` inserts a value, `%%` is a percent sign, `""` a quote.
entries.example: send "Sale: 50%% off for %player%" to player
entries.name: Text

entries.description: Changes letter case.
entries.example: send "%capitalized "steve"%" to player
entries.name: Text case

entries.description: Fields of a text display entity: alignment `left`, `center` or `right`, line width in pixels (default 200) and text opacity 0 to 255 (default 255). Can be set; width and opacity can be added to, removed from and reset.
entries.example:
spawn text display at player with text "hi"
set text alignment of last spawned entity to left
entries.name: Text display alignment, line width, opacity

entries.description: A length of time, like `1 hour and 30 seconds`.
entries.example: set {delay} to 1 minute and 30 seconds
entries.name: Timespan

entries.description: One part of a timespan, the same as `minutes of {t}`.
entries.example:
set {_t} to 2 minutes and 30 seconds
send "%{_t}'s minutes%:%{_t}'s seconds%" to player
entries.name: Timespan part ('s form)

entries.description: One part of a timespan, or the whole span in that unit with `total`.
entries.example:
set {_t} to 1 hour and 30 minutes
send "%total minutes of {_t}%" to player
entries.name: Timespan parts

entries.description: A timespan as words, like `1 hour and 5 minutes`. Plain `formatted` gives `1:05:00`.
entries.example: send "%{_t} formatted human-readable%"
entries.name: Timespan, human readable

entries.description: The title, style and viewers of a boss bar, and the title and viewers of an inventory value. Add or remove players from viewers to show, hide, open or close; the title of an inventory in a variable can be set.
entries.name: Title, style, viewers

entries.description: The item in the main hand, `air` when empty.
entries.example:
if tool of player is diamond sword:
    send "nice sword" to player
entries.name: Tool

entries.description: The player's UUID as text. Good for variable names.
entries.example: add 1 to {joins::%uuid of player%}
entries.name: UUID

entries.description: A global (saved) or local (`_`) variable. `<none>` when never set.
entries.example: set {_x} to {coins::%uuid of player%}
entries.name: Variable

entries.description: `w of q` reads the w part of a quaternion (`x`, `y`, `z` work on vectors and quaternions). `set`, `add` and `remove` change one part of a vector or quaternion variable. Yaw and pitch turn a vector (keeping its length), a player or an entity.
entries.name: Vector and quaternion components

entries.description: The entity something rides, and the list of entities riding it. Read only.
entries.example: set {_v} to vehicle of player
entries.name: Vehicle and passengers

entries.description: Villager data: level and experience as numbers, the profession as text like `librarian` or `none`. Read only.
entries.example: set {_lvl} to villager level of last spawned entity
entries.name: Villager level, experience and profession

entries.description: Whether the whitelist is on, switching it, and the list of whitelisted players.
entries.example:
set whitelist to true
set {_w::*} to whitelisted players
entries.name: Whitelist state and players

entries.description: A world by name, or the world of a location or player.
entries.example:
if world of player is "world":
    send "overworld" to player
entries.name: World

entries.description: The world border of a world (the default world when none is given), and its warning distance (blocks) and warning time (a timespan). The warnings can be set, added to, removed from and reset.
entries.example:
set world border warning distance to 10
add 30 seconds to world border warning time
entries.name: World border

entries.description: The center (a location at y 0), the damage per block outside the border and the safe distance past it. A world works in place of its border. Can be set, reset, and the numbers added to or removed from.
entries.example:
set world border center of world border of world of player to location(0, 0, 0)
set world border damage amount of world of player to 1
entries.name: World border center and damage

entries.description: `true` or `false` (also `yes` and `no`).
entries.name: Boolean

entries.description: A chunk by its chunk coordinates, or the chunk a location is in. Can be stored and compared.
entries.example: send "%chunk of location(17, 64, -1)%"
entries.name: Chunk

entries.description: A color. Write a dye color (`red`, `light blue`), `rgb(r, g, b)` (0 to 255) or `color from hex "#rrggbb"`. Prints as `#rrggbb`, so `red value of` and the other channel expressions work on it.
entries.example:
send "%hex of rgb(255, 128, 0)%"
send "%red value of lime%"
entries.name: Color

entries.description: A moment in time, in UTC.
entries.name: Date

entries.description: An item type with an amount. Compares by type, not amount.
entries.name: Item

entries.description: A list parameter or result in a function. The element type is not checked.
entries.name: List

entries.description: A point with x, y, z and an optional world. Blocks are locations with whole numbers.
entries.name: Location

entries.description: About sixty types whose values are a fixed list of names: click type, damage cause, tree type, moon phase, spawn reason, potion effect type, and so on (full list on the page). Write a value as plain words, or make it from text with `parsed as`. A value equals text with the same name and works as a function parameter type.
entries.example:
function describe(c: click type) :: text:
    return "click: %{_c}%"
on join:
    send describe(shift left)
    set {_m} to "waxing crescent" parsed as moon phase
    send "%{_m}%"
entries.name: Named values

entries.description: Whole or decimal numbers, like `5` or `-2.5`.
entries.name: Number

entries.description: Any value. Checked when the line runs.
entries.name: Object

entries.description: An online player. Prints as the name.
entries.name: Player

entries.description: A rotation as w, x, y, z. Can be stored, compared and passed to functions.
entries.example:
set {q} to quaternion(1, 0, 0, 0)
send "%{q}%"
entries.name: Quaternion

entries.description: A first-in-first-out collection made from values. Prints its items; not saved in variables.json.
entries.example: send "%queue(1, 2, 3)%"
entries.name: Queue

entries.description: Text in quotes. A text slot accepts any value and prints it.
entries.name: Text

entries.description: A stretch of the day between two times, in ticks (0 is 6:00, 12000 is 18:00).
entries.example: send "%timeperiod(0, 12000)%"
entries.name: Timeperiod

entries.description: A length of time in milliseconds. One tick is 50 ms.
entries.name: Timespan

entries.description: A 3D direction or offset with x, y and z, like `vector(0, 1, 0)`.
entries.name: Vector

entries.description: A world. Equals text with its name.
entries.name: World

entries.description: The world border of a world, as a value you can keep in a variable. Size is read and set with the world border size forms.
entries.example: set {b} to world border of world of player
entries.name: World border

entries.description: The number without its minus sign.
entries.example: send "%abs(-3)%" to player
entries.name: abs

entries.description: Keeps a number between two bounds; median and product take numbers or a list.
entries.example: send "%clamp(15, 0, 10)%" to player
entries.name: clamp, median, product

entries.description: Text helpers: join values, format a number with a pattern, convert between bases, build a hex colour, parse a UUID.
entries.example: send "%toBase(255, 16)%" to player
entries.name: concat, formatNumber, toBase, fromBase, rgb, uuid

entries.description: Exponent, logarithms, roots and counting functions. `log` is base 10 unless a base is given.
entries.example: send "%combinations(5, 2)%" to player
entries.name: exp, ln, log, root, factorial, combinations, permutations, isNaN

entries.description: Rounds down, up, or to the nearest whole number. `round(n, places)` keeps that many decimal places.
entries.example: send "%round(2.6)% %round(3.14159, 2)%" to player
entries.name: floor / ceil / round

entries.description: Makes a location, optionally in a world.
entries.example: teleport player to location(0, 64, 0)
entries.name: location

entries.description: The smallest or biggest of two or more numbers.
entries.example: send "%max(3, 7, 5)%" to player
entries.name: min / max

entries.description: Remainder, always 0 or more: `mod(-1, 5)` is 4.
entries.example: send "%mod(7, 3)%" to player
entries.name: mod

entries.description: Looks a player up by name or UUID, and gives the experience points a level needs.
entries.example: send "%calcExperience(10)%" to player
entries.name: player, offlinePlayer, calcExperience

entries.description: Defines a function callable from any script, as a value or on its own line. A script function wins over a built-in with the same name.
entries.example:
function coins(p: player) :: number:
    return {coins::%uuid of {_p}%} ? 0
on join:
    send "%coins(player)% coins" to player
entries.name: Script functions

entries.description: Trigonometry in degrees. The inverse functions return degrees.
entries.example: send "%sin(30)%" to player
entries.name: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2

entries.description: Square root. A negative number is an error.
entries.example: send "%sqrt(16)%" to player
entries.name: sqrt
